381155.title: Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for rainbow triangles
381155.literal_statement:
Let $r$ and $t$ be positive integers, and let $r(t)$ denote the two-color Ramsey number: the least integer $m$ such that every $2$-coloring of the edges of the complete graph on $m$ vertices contains a monochromatic clique of order $t$. Define

$$
N(r,t)=\left(r(t)-1\right)^{r/2}
$$

when $r$ is even, and

$$
N(r,t)=(t-1)\left(r(t)-1\right)^{(r-1)/2}
$$

when $r$ is odd. A coloring of the edges of a complete graph is a **rainbow triangle** if some triangle has three differently colored edges, and a **monochromatic $K_t$** is a complete subgraph on $t$ vertices whose edges all have one color. **Erdős–Hajnal conjecture.** For $n>N(r,t)$, every $r$-coloring of the edges of the complete graph on $n$ vertices has a rainbow triangle or a monochromatic $K_t$.

This conjecture asserts that the lexicographic-product constructions described in the paper give the best possible bounds for avoiding both rainbow triangles and monochromatic cliques. It was verified by Chung and Graham in the case $t=3$; the general case remains open in the supplied source.

326412.title: De Loera–Lee–Margulies–Miller conjecture on minor-minimal non-weakly-orientable matroids
326412.literal_statement:
Let $M\!I_n$ be the infinite family of matroids constructed in the paper, indexed by integers $n\geq 0$. A matroid is **weakly orientable** when its Bland–Jensen linear system has a solution over $F_2$; it is **minor-minimal non-weakly-orientable** when it is non-weakly orientable but every proper minor is weakly orientable. The authors conjecture that

**Minor-minimality conjecture.** For all integers $n\geq 0$, $M\!I_n$ are minor-minimal with respect to being non-weakly-orientable. Hence, weak-orientability cannot be described by a finite list of excluded minors.

The family $M\!I_n$ is an infinite family of non-weakly-orientable matroids with growing rank and corank. The authors checked explicitly that $M\!I_n$ is minor-minimal for $n\leq 2$; the conjecture would imply the earlier Bland–Jensen conjecture that weak orientability cannot be characterized by a finite list of excluded minors.

326795.title: The conjecture on unicentroidal trees with edge-reconstruction number 3
326795.literal_statement:
Let $\text{ern}(G)$ denote the edge-reconstruction number of a graph $G$, namely the minimum number of edge-deleted subgraphs $G-e$ sufficient to determine $G$ up to isomorphism. A tree is **unicentroidal** if it has a single centroid.

**The unicentroidal edge-reconstruction conjecture.** The only infinite classes of unicentroidal trees which have $\text{ern}=3$ are the paths on an odd number of vertices, the caterpillars $C(2,0,\ldots,0,2)$ of even diameter, and the family of trees $T_k$ depicted in Figure.

The paper reports these three infinite families from computer searches and conjectures that no other infinite families of unicentroidal trees have edge-reconstruction number 3. The surrounding results establish the corresponding classification for bicentroidal trees apart from three stated exceptions; the conjecture concerns the remaining unicentroidal case.

330886.title: Non-embeddability conjecture for De Bruijn and Kautz graphs
330886.literal_statement:
Let $Br(m,n)$ be the undirected De Bruijn graph on $m^n$ words of length $n$, with edges joining $(a_1\dots a_n)$ to $(a_2\dots a_na_{n+1})$. Let $Ka(m,n)$ be the undirected Kautz graph on length-$n$ words with consecutive symbols distinct, with the analogous edges. Here, $2$-tr.embeddability is the embedding property used in the paper.

**De Bruijn–Kautz non-embeddability conjecture.** (i) All $Br(m,n)$ with $(m,n)\neq(2,2)$ are not $2$-tr.embeddable. (ii) All $Ka(m,n)$ with $m\geq 3$ are not $2$-tr.embeddable.

The exceptional graph $Br(2,2)=K_4-e$ embeds into $\frac{1}{2}H_4$, while $Ka(2,n)=K_2=H_1$. The stated cases have been checked computationally for the finite parameter lists given in the source.

323970.title: Berge–Jackson–Zhang conjecture on circuit double covers
323970.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph. A **circuit double cover** (CDC) is a set of circuits such that every edge of $G$ is covered by exactly two circuits. A graph is **cyclically $5$-edge-connected** if no edge cut of size less than $5$ separates two circuits.

**Berge–Jackson–Zhang conjecture.** If $G$ is a cyclically $5$-edge-connected cubic graph and $D$ is a set of pairwise disjoint circuits of $G$, then $D$ is a subset of a CDC, unless $G$ is the Petersen graph.

The paper states that its construction yields counterexamples to this conjecture: the relevant permutation $2$-factor is not contained in any circuit double cover. Earlier finite counterexamples were also found by computer search.

330940.title: The cherry-count conjecture for random tanglegrams
330940.literal_statement: A **cherry** is a pair of leaves joined to a common parent in a binary tree. Let a tanglegram of size $n$ be chosen uniformly at random, and consider its left binary tree. **Cherry-count conjecture.** The expected number of cherries in the left tree converges to $n/4$ as $n$ tends to infinity. This predicts linear growth for the expected number of cherries in a random tanglegram; the source presents it as suggested by computer experiments and does not state a proof.

325964.title: Theta-number conjecture for 1-intersecting invertible matrices
325964.literal_statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $\Gamma=\operatorname{GL}(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$, and let

$$
G_{q,n,1}=\operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,X_{q,n,1}),\qquad X_{q,n,1}=\{A\in\operatorname{GL}(n,\mathbb{F}_q):\operatorname{rank}(A-I)>n-1\}.
$$

Here $\alpha(G)$ denotes the independence number and $\vartheta(G)$ the Lovász theta-number. **Theta-number conjecture.** For all values of $n$ and $q$,

$$
\vartheta(G_{q,n,1})=\alpha(G_{q,n,1})=\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}(q^n-q^i).
$$

The product is attained by the family of invertible matrices fixing a chosen nonzero vector. The equality was verified numerically for small values of $n$ and $q$, but the assertion for all parameters remains open.

330457.title: The forbidden-subgraph characterization conjecture for dominating induced matchings
330457.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a finite set of graphs. Let $\cal S$ be the class of graphs whose connected components are graphs $S_{i,j,k}$. An $M$-free graph is a graph containing no induced subgraph isomorphic to a graph in $M$.

**Forbidden-subgraph characterization conjecture.** Unless $P=NP$, the dominating induced matching problem is polynomial-time solvable in the class of $M$-free graphs if and only if $M$ contains a graph from $\cal S$.

This conjecture proposes that the known necessary condition for polynomial-time solvability on finitely characterized graph classes is also sufficient. The parser marks the conjecture as disproved, although the supplied surrounding text only says that proving or disproving it is challenging; the resolution evidence should therefore be checked.

338717.title: Conjecture on polynomial-time enumeration of regular graphs
338717.literal_statement:
Fix $k
greater than or equal to 1$ and let $a_n$ be the number of unlabeled $k$-regular graphs with $n$ vertices.

**Regular-graph enumeration conjecture.** The sequence $a_n$ can be computed in polynomial time in $n$.

The source notes polynomial recurrences for labeled $k$-regular graphs for each fixed $k$, but does not establish the corresponding claim for unlabeled graphs. No resolution is supplied.

354781.title: Cilleruelo–Córdoba's truncated square-frequency conjecture
354781.literal_statement:
Let $\gamma\in(0,1)$ be fixed, let $N$ be positive, and let $f$ be a trigonometric polynomial whose frequencies lie in $\{n^2:N\leqslant n\leqslant N+N^\gamma\}$. **Cilleruelo–Córdoba's conjecture.** One has

$$
\|f\|_4\ll_\gamma\|f\|_2.
$$

The assertion is known for $\gamma\leqslant1/2$ because the relevant square set is Sidon. The paper proves it for every $\gamma<\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}$, leaving the range above that threshold open.

354874.title: Thrackle-style conjecture for almost holey convex families
354874.literal_statement:
Suppose that $d4c2$ is a set of $n$ points in the plane, and let $S_1,cdots,S_m\subseteq d4c2$ be subsets with convex hulls

$$
C_i=\operatorname{conv}(S_i).
$$

Assume that $1<|S_i|<n$ for every $i$, that $C_i\cap C_j\ne\emptyset$ whenever $i\ne j$, and that

$$
C_i\cap C_j\cap C_k\subseteq d4c2
$$

whenever $i\ne j\ne k\ne i$. **Thrackle-style conjecture for almost holey convex families.** Under these assumptions, $m\le n$. This is posed as an open problem for families of pairwise-intersecting convex hulls whose triple intersections contain only the given points; the paper does not provide a resolution.

354926.title: Fastest-convergence conjecture for the complementing flip process
354926.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{R}$ be a convergent flip process of order $k$ with a single destination. For $\delta\in(0,\frac{1}{2})$, let $\tau_{\mathcal{R}}^-(\delta)$ denote its lower convergence time.

**Fastest-convergence conjecture.** For every such $\mathcal{R}$ and every $\delta\in(0,\frac{1}{2})$,

$$
\tau_{\mathcal{R}}^-(\delta)\ge \frac{-\ln(2\delta)}{2(k)_2}.
$$

The bound is attained by the complementing flip process, whose convergence time is described in the source as half that of an ignorant process with output density $1/2$. The source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

354961.title: Shangguan's generic Vandermonde full-rank conjecture
354961.literal_statement:
Let $[t]=\{1,\ldots,t\}$ and let $J_1,\ldots,J_t\subseteq[n]$ satisfy, for every $S\subseteq[t]$,

$$
\sum_{i\in S}|J_i|-\left|\bigcup_{i\in S}J_i\right|\leqslant (|S|-1)k.
$$

Assume also that the corresponding inequality is an equality for $S=[t]$. Let $G$ be a generic $(n,k)$-Vandermonde matrix, and let $M_{G,(J_1,\ldots,J_t)}$ be the matrix defined in the source from $G$ and these subsets.

**Shangguan's full-rank conjecture.** The matrix $M_{G,(J_1,\ldots,J_t)}$ has full column rank.

The conjecture is formulated as a rank criterion whose resolution would imply that generic Reed–Solomon codes achieve list-decoding capacity. The source does not provide evidence of a resolution, so its status is open.

354963.title: Finite principal-specialization conjecture for chromatic symmetric functions of trees
354963.literal_statement:
Let $N$ be a positive integer, let $q$ be an indeterminate, and let $T$ and $U$ be trees with at most $N+1$ vertices. Write $X_T(1,q,q^2,\ldots,q^N)$ for the principal specialization of the chromatic symmetric function of $T$.

**Finite principal-specialization conjecture.** For all such trees,

$$
T\cong U \quad\text{if and only if}\quad X_T(1,q,q^2,\ldots,q^N)=X_U(1,q,q^2,\ldots,q^N).
$$

The parser provides no resolution evidence for this finite version; it is presented in the paper as a conjectural analogue arising from principal specialization.

355013.title: Schnetz's prime reduction conjecture for $c_2$ invariants
355013.literal_statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be graphs, and for a prime power $q=p^s$ let $c_2^{(q)}(G)$ denote their $c_2$ invariants. **Schnetz's prime reduction conjecture.** If

$$
c_2^{(p)}(G_1)\equiv c_2^{(p)}(G_2)\pmod p
$$

for every prime $p$, then

$$
c_2^{(q)}(G_1)\equiv c_2^{(q)}(G_2)\pmod q
$$

for every prime power $q=p^s$. The conjecture would reduce comparisons of $c_2$ invariants at all prime powers to comparisons at primes. The source attributes this conjecture to Oliver Schnetz and presents it as an open question.

355016.title: Categorical genericity conjecture for the combinatorial derived matroid
355016.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a representable matroid with set of circuits $\mathcal{C}$. For matroids on a fixed ground set, use the **weak order** defined by $M_1\geq M_2$ when every dependent set of $M_1$ is dependent in $M_2$. **Categorical genericity conjecture.** Then

$$
\delta M\geq\delta_{OW}(R)
$$

for every representation $R$ of $M$, where the order is the weak order on matroids with ground set $\mathcal{C}$. This claims that the combinatorial derived matroid is the generic, maximal derived matroid in the categorical weak-order sense.

355426.title: Common-factor conjecture for numerators of triangular-grid edge resistances
355426.literal_statement:
Let $L_s^{(i)}$, for $i\in\{1,2\}$, be the edge-resistance quantities defined in the paper, and let $\operatorname{num}(x)$ denote the numerator of the maximally reduced fractional representation of $x$. Let $\gcd$ denote the greatest common divisor. **Common-factor conjecture.** For every integer $s\geq 1$,

$$
\gcd\bigl(\operatorname{num}(L_s^{(1)}),\operatorname{num}(L_{s+1}^{(2)})\bigr)>1.
$$

This conjecture predicts a persistent arithmetic relation between numerators of resistance values in successive transformed rims. The supplied text gives no evidence that it has been proved or disproved.

355433.title: The number characterization conjecture for bidding games
355433.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a bidding game. A **subposition** $H$ of $G$ has Left options $H^L$ and Right options $H^R$.

**Number characterization conjecture.** The following are equivalent:

1. $H^L < H^R$ for every subposition $H$ of $G$ and every $H^L$ and $H^R$.
2. $H^L < H < H^R$ for every subposition $H$ of $G$ and every $H^L$ and $H^R$.

The conjecture proposes an equivalence between the usual option-separation condition and the stronger condition that every subposition lies strictly between its Left and Right options. The paper states that this is expected to agree with the definition of a number used for alternating play; no resolution is supplied here.

355433.ordinary_attempt_failure_or_exclusion: Reverse implication is strict-order transitivity. Forward birthday induction gives number options but not interpolation of H. Inverse translation still needs a 0-bid strategy for all contexts/partitions; standalone outcomes and marker monotonicity do not establish it. No contextual witness or general strategy proved; see ORDINARY.md.
